subject: Data retention exception request - log retention and PII controls
messages:
From: Emily Johnson <emily.johnson@acmepay.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: data retention & PII controls (Acme Payments)

Hi Rafael / Camila,

Thanks again for the call this morning - great overview of Redwood and how you handle inference at scale. As promised, attaching a short summary of the retention requirements from our privacy team (acme_data_retention_request.pdf). Key asks:

- We need a "zero-retention" option for any logs that contain PII (names, email addresses, payment IDs). These logs must not be retained after initial processing.
- For non-PII telemetry (anonymized usage/metrics), we can accept a shorter retention window (30 days).
- All logs must reside in US data centers (us-east preferred) and never leave US regions.
- We need an audit trail showing deletion or retention actions for compliance.

Can you confirm whether these options are feasible and what the typical timeline would be to implement an exception/addendum? Also copied Daniel from legal if he has follow-ups.

Thanks,
Emily Johnson
Privacy Ops - Acme Payments
emily.johnson@acmepay.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Emily Johnson <emily.johnson@acmepay.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-05T13:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: data retention & PII controls (Acme Payments)

Emily - thanks for the clear doc and for joining the call. I pulled together a short recap and proposed next steps below. Looping in Neha (security) to validate technical implications and Marissa for commercial/contracting.

Recap of asks:
- Zero-retention for logs containing PII (no persistent storage).
- 30-day retention for anonymized usage metrics.
- US-only residency (us-east preferred).
- Audit trail for deletion actions.

Initial feasibility notes (high level):
- Zero-retention for PII: we can support on a per-route basis by disabling persistent logging and ensuring any ephemeral caches are wiped post-request. Need Security to confirm edge cases (e.g., troubleshooting traces, error logs).
- Shortened retention (30 days) for anonymized metrics: straightforward via retention policy configuration.
- Data residency: we can scope logs to a specific region for Dedicated/Private customers; hosted customers can be pinned to region where supported.
- Audit trails: we can emit a deletion event and store an immutable audit record (can be included in SOC2 evidence) - will need to confirm retention length of audit records with Legal.

Proposed next steps:
1) Neha to provide technical constraints and any required controls we must keep for safety/diagnostics.
2) Redwood legal to draft a retention addendum / exception (Marissa).
3) Demo of the retention config & delete flow (I can set up a short session with our infra team).
4) Target timeline: initial legal draft + technical short-list in 5 business days.

Attachments: redwood_retention_policy_summary.pdf (high-level options).

Would you be available for a 30-minute follow-up next week?

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive - Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Johnson <emily.johnson@acmepay.com>
Date: 2028-04-06T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: data retention & PII controls (Acme Payments)

Thanks Rafael - quick security read. High-level feasibility looks good but a few important items to flag/questions we need answered from Acme:

1) Definition of PII: please confirm which fields you consider PII vs. pseudonymous identifiers. E.g., is a masked payment token PII? We need explicit list to implement field-level redaction.
2) Troubleshooting & support: with zero-retention enabled for PII, our ability to perform post-incident debugging will be limited. We can offer an opt-in support window where traces are kept for X hours and then purged; need Acme's sign-off.
3) KV cache & model context: model-side KV caches may contain user-provided context. We can avoid persisting any KV to durable storage, but if you use Dedicated/Private we recommend configuring instance-level ephemeral storage cleared on rotate.
4) Audit logs: we propose keeping immutable audit entries for deletion actions for 1 year (these contain hashed identifiers only). Please let us know if Acme requires a different timeline.
5) Data residency: confirmed we can constrain to us-east for hosted customers where capacity exists; Dedicated/Private gives stricter control.

Action items for Redwood:
- Provide a short tech spec for how zero-retention is enforced (field redaction, ephemeral pipeline) - I will draft this in 2 business days.
- List of support trade-offs and a proposed short retention window for traces (suggest 72 hours for critical traces).

Neha
Security Engineer - Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

From: Emily Johnson <emily.johnson@acmepay.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Park <dpark@acmepay.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-07T08:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: data retention & PII controls (Acme Payments)

Hi all - thanks for the quick responses. A few clarifications from our privacy/legal teams (answers inline):

- Definition of PII: fields we must treat as PII are full names, email addresses, unmasked payment IDs, full address. Masked tokens (last4) are acceptable as non-PII. We will share a definitive field list in the attached acme_sc_requirements.xlsx.
- Support/troubleshooting: Acme can accept a short support window of 48 hours where traces may be retained for debugging (we expect explicit logging and deletion events). After 48 hours, traces containing PII must be purged.
- Audit logs: Acme requires audit evidence of deletion actions for 12 months. Hashes are acceptable for identification in the audit trail.
- Data residency: us-east is fine.

We are comfortable moving forward if Redwood can:
1) Implement zero-retention for PII with a 48-hour emergency-troubleshoot window.
2) Configure anonymized metrics to 30-day retention.
3) Provide yearly audit entries (hashed) showing deletion actions.
4) Add an addendum to the contract describing the above.

Attached: acme_sc_requirements.xlsx (field list).

Thanks,
Emily

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Emily Johnson <emily.johnson@acmepay.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-10T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed next steps & action plan - Acme Payments retention exception

Emily / Daniel - appreciate the clarity. Based on Neha's notes and your confirmations, here's a proposed mutual action plan and timeline:

1) Tech spec: Redwood to deliver a short technical spec documenting how zero-retention is implemented (field-level redaction, ephemeral pipelines, KV cache policies) - delivery by 2028-04-12. (Owner: Neha)
2) Support window: implement an opt-in 48-hour troubleshooting retention for PII traces. This will be a per-route flag that Acme signs off on. (Owner: Product/Infra)
3) Retention config: anonymized metrics set to 30 days by default. (Owner: Infra)
4) Audit trail: Redwood will provide hashed deletion audit records retained for 12 months. Format and access method to be included in the spec. (Owner: Security/Compliance)
4) Legal: Marissa to prepare a contract addendum / retention exception that captures these items and the acceptance conditions. Target draft by 2028-04-14.
5) Follow-up: 30-minute review session to walk through the tech spec and the addendum, scheduled week of 2028-04-17.

Links: HubSpot deal (https://redwood.hubspot.com/deal/RD-2028-0453) and initial draft retention summary attached (redwood_retention_policy_summary.pdf).

If that timeline works, I'll ask Legal to open the addendum draft and set a DocuSign flow.

Best,
Rafael

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Johnson <emily.johnson@acmepay.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-10T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed next steps & action plan - Acme Payments retention exception

Thanks team - sounds good. Marissa / Legal, please prioritize the addendum draft so we can get this into a DocuSign flow. Rafael - pls set up the 30-minute review for week of 4/17; I'll bring the commercial terms for the Dedicated reservation if Acme wants dedicated capacity for strict residency.

Camila Reyes
Senior Solutions Engineer - Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com
